title: Compact density: inversion-safe token set and component overrides for high-density dark variants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Define a compact-density token set and corresponding component overrides that remain visually stable under color inversion or extreme contrast settings. This work is targeted at console views where high information density is required (dense tables, narrow sidebars, mini-charts) and where brand theming must not break readability or interaction affordances in dark or high-contrast environments. Outcome: a documented token subset, component override rules for buttons/tables/charts, implementation guidance for designers and engineers, and a migration path for existing console screens.
acceptance_criteria: Token set includes neutral elevation tokens, two inversion-safe foreground scales, and two tint-preserving brand accents for dense UI
Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost) render legible labels at 12px/14px across contrast modes and pass WCAG AA text contrast for normal text sizes
Table zebra and grid separators adapt to dark dense surfaces without introducing perceptual noise; delta between row backgrounds adheres to contrast guidance
Mini line and sparkline charts maintain stroke visibility against inverted backgrounds and when overlaid on density surfaces
Design tokens are documented in Figma and exported JSON mapping for engineering with clear fallback rules and platform hints
Migration guide and rollout checklist published; can toggle new tokens behind a UI feature flag for experimentation
decisions: Use inverted-neutral tokens (surface-02..surface-04) rather than single 'surface' token to avoid mid-tone banding on mini-charts
Prefer semi-transparent overlays for separators (alpha over surface) instead of hard color shifts to preserve texture on dense rows
Brand accents for compact mode will map to two saturation tiers: accent-compact and accent-compact-muted, with explicit luminance targets for dark variants
Do not change existing global token names; supply a 'compact' token namespace (compact.surface-1, compact.fg-1) and migration aliases handled in runtime
open_questions: Should compact token namespace be opt-in per route or globally enable via feature flag? (trade-off: per-route reduces blast radius but increases engineering surface)
How to express line-height and letter-spacing adjustments for dense button labels in token exports (should they live in tokens or component overrides)?
Do we want to support automatic tint-shifting for user-uploaded brand colors or require curated brand palette entries for compact mode?
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created by Maya. Initial research notes and Figma file linked.
2026-02-26: Spike with Eng (Benji Kaur) showed minor shader artifact on sparkline when using alpha separators—moved to decision to use semi-transparent overlays.
2026-03-03: Accessibility review (Lina Ortiz) recommended increasing min contrast for compact.fg-1 to 4.5:1 for 12px labels; updated acceptance criteria.
2026-03-08: Scoped rollout plan added: behind 'compact-theme' feature flag, A/B test on 10% of workspaces, telemetry to capture token-related regressions.
2026-03-10: PR opened by ENG-21410: add compact token JSON and mapping functions; awaiting review. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7142
implementation_notes: Engineering to expose 'themeDensity' param in client config (values: default | compact). Renderer to resolve compact token namespace before fallback to global tokens.
Provide a small JS utility 'mapCompactBrandAccent(brandColor)' that returns two computed accents with constrained luminance for dark mode.
Charts: prefer stroke-width scaling (0.5->1.0) and additive glow on hover rather than increasing stroke contrast to avoid overpowering dense content
Tables: use a single px hairline divider with soft alpha; avoid heavy shadows or elevation on dense surfaces to keep visual rhythm
qa_checklist: Render sample dense views (3 system pages) in light/dark/high-contrast and compact/default density
Run color contrast checks on all button permutations and table rows for 12/14px label sizes
Verify Figma tokens export matches engineering JSON exactly
Smoke test feature flag toggle across routes to ensure no flash of default tokens
